question: Ambubachi Mela (Fair) is held in which of the temples of North-East India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamakhya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ambubachi Mela is an annual Hindu festival celebrated at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam. (कामाख्या मंदिर — अंबुबाची मेला)

 

• It celebrates the yearly menstruation course of goddess Kamakhya, a form of Shakti/Devi, and is also called the "Ameti" or "Tantric fertility festival".

 

• The Kamakhya Temple is one of the oldest of the 51 Shakti Peethas and is situated on the Nilachal Hill near Guwahati.

 

• During the mela, held in the Assamese month of Ahaar (mid-June, coinciding with the monsoon), the temple remains closed for three days and reopens with great celebration.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kamakhya Temple's present structure was rebuilt in 1565 after being destroyed by Kala Pahar, with patronage from Koch King Naranarayana.

 

• Assam is also home to other important Shakti temples and is a major centre of Tantric worship.

 

NOTE

 

• Dakshineswar Kali (Option 1): This temple is located on the banks of the Hooghly River in West Bengal, not North-East India.

 

• Bhuvaneswari (Option 2): This is actually a shrine located within the Kamakhya temple complex itself, not a separate temple where Ambubachi Mela is held.

 

• Billeswar (Option 3): This is a Shiva temple in Assam, not the venue of the Ambubachi Mela.

question: Which of the following groups of states recorded very high population growth rate during 2001-2011 Census of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census, the states with the highest decadal population growth rate (2001-2011) were Meghalaya (27.95%), Arunachal Pradesh (26.03%) and Bihar (25.42%). (जनसंख्या वृद्धि दर — मेघालय, अरुणाचल प्रदेश, बिहार)

 

• India's overall decadal growth rate for 2001-2011 was 17.64%, the lowest since independence up to that point.

 

• Nagaland was the only state to register a negative growth rate (-0.47%) during this decade.

 

• Kerala recorded one of the lowest positive growth rates (4.91%) among major states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uttar Pradesh remained India's most populous state as per Census 2011, followed by Maharashtra and Bihar.

 

• Sikkim recorded a relatively low decadal growth rate of about 12.36% in this period, a sharp fall from the previous decade.

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar, Rajasthan, Sikkim (Option 1): Rajasthan (21.44%) and Sikkim (12.36%) did not record among the very highest growth rates.

 

• West Bengal, Meghalaya, Bihar (Option 2): West Bengal's growth rate (13.84%) was well below the top group.

 

• Bihar, Haryana, Meghalaya (Option 3): Haryana's growth rate (19.9%) was lower than Arunachal Pradesh's, so it does not belong to the top three.

question: A wealthy person in the early Vedic period was known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gomat.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Early Vedic period, wealth was measured primarily in terms of cattle (cows), since the Vedic economy was pastoral. A wealthy person, i.e., one who possessed many cows, was called "Gomat". (गोमत — प्रारंभिक वैदिक काल का धनी व्यक्ति)

 

• The word derives from "Go", meaning cow, which was the chief unit of wealth and exchange in this era.

 

• Terms such as "Gaveshna" (a search/expedition for cows, often linked to war/battle — literally "desire for cows") and "Gavishti" also reflect the centrality of cattle in Vedic society and economy.

 

• Cattle raids (Gavishti) were a common cause of inter-tribal conflict in this period, underlining cows as the primary measure of wealth and status.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Early Vedic period (c. 1500-1000 BCE) economy was largely pastoral and semi-nomadic, based on cattle rearing, unlike the more settled agrarian economy of the Later Vedic period.

 

• A daughter in the Vedic texts was sometimes referred to as "Duhitri" (one who milks the cow), reflecting the same cattle-centred worldview.

 

NOTE

 

• Duhitri (Option 1): This term refers to a daughter (literally "one who milks"), not a wealthy person.

 

• Gaveshna (Option 2): This term refers to the search for cows/cattle raid, often associated with warfare, not to a wealthy individual.

 

• Ravi (Option 4): This term refers to the sun, unrelated to wealth or cattle.

question: India has been ranked ______ in the Medical Tourism Index (MTI) for 2020-21 out of 46 destinations by the Medical Tourism Association.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India was ranked 10th in the Medical Tourism Index (MTI) 2020-21, released by the Medical Tourism Association (MTA), among 46 destinations globally. (चिकित्सा पर्यटन सूचकांक — भारत 10वां स्थान)

 

• The index evaluates countries on parameters like quality of facilities and services, industry and destination environment, and cost of medical tourism.

 

• Canada topped the 2020-21 Medical Tourism Index.

 

• India's improving rank reflects its growing reputation for affordable, quality healthcare for international patients, especially in cardiac care, orthopaedics and organ transplants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has also launched initiatives like the "Heal in India" programme and Ayush Visa category to boost medical and wellness tourism.

 

• Major Indian medical tourism hubs include Chennai, Delhi-NCR, Mumbai and Bengaluru.

 

NOTE

 

• 15th, 20th, 5th (Options 2, 3, 4): These do not match India's officially reported rank of 10th in the MTI 2020-21.

question: The Japfu range, which is 3,014 meters high, is located in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagaland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mount Japfu, at an elevation of about 3,014 metres (9,890 feet), is located in Nagaland, near the state capital Kohima. (जफू पर्वत — नागालैंड)

 

• It is the second-highest peak in Nagaland after Mount Saramati, and one of the highest peaks in the Naga Hills.

 

• The mountain is famous for hosting one of the world's tallest rhododendron trees and is a popular trekking destination.

 

• It lies close to Kigwema village, about 15 km from Kohima.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mount Saramati (3,826 m) is the highest peak in Nagaland and also the highest point in the entire Naga Hills-Patkai range.

 

• Nagaland's terrain is part of the Purvanchal (Eastern Hills) range of the Himalayas.

 

NOTE

 

• Assam (Option 1): Assam is largely a plains state (Brahmaputra and Barak valleys) and does not contain the Japfu range.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 2): This state has its own high Himalayan peaks like Kangto, but not the Japfu range.

 

• Meghalaya (Option 3): Meghalaya's highest point is Shillong Peak (~1,965 m), much lower and unrelated to Japfu.

question: Who among the following performing artists bagged the best actress award for Meena Gurjari in 1975?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mallika Sarabhai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mallika Sarabhai, the noted Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, made her acting debut with the Gujarati film "Mena Gurjari" (1975), for which she won a Best Actress award. (मल्लिका साराभाई — मेना गुर्जरी, सर्वश्रेष्ठ अभिनेत्री पुरस्कार 1975)

 

• She is the daughter of noted scientist Vikram Sarabhai and classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai.

 

• Mallika Sarabhai is primarily renowned as a classical dancer, choreographer and social activist, and heads the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad.

 

• She was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2010 for her contribution to the arts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mallika Sarabhai has also performed internationally, notably in Peter Brook's stage production of the Mahabharata.

 

• She is known for using dance and theatre as a medium for social and political activism.

 

NOTE

 

• Sonal Mansingh (Option 1): A renowned Odissi and Bharatanatyam exponent and Padma Vibhushan awardee, not associated with Mena Gurjari.

 

• Sitara Devi (Option 2): A legendary Kathak dancer, not associated with this film.

 

• Shovana Narayan (Option 3): A prominent Kathak dancer, not associated with this film.

question: Urmila Satyanarayanan is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Urmila Satyanarayanan is a well-known exponent of Bharatanatyam, trained under the renowned guru K. N. Dandayudhapani Pillai. (उर्मिला सत्यनारायणन — भरतनाट्यम)

 

• She heads the Sathya Dance Academy in Chennai and is known for both her performing and teaching career in Bharatanatyam.

 

• She has been honoured with several awards for her contribution to classical dance, including recognition from the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

 

• Bharatanatyam itself originated in Tamil Nadu and is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, rooted in the Natya Shastra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Bharatanatyam exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Alarmel Valli.

 

• The classical repertoire of Bharatanatyam is called the "Margam", comprising items like Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam and Tillana.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 2): A classical dance form of North India, associated with dancers like Birju Maharaj and Sitara Devi.

 

• Manipuri (Option 3): A classical dance form from Manipur, associated with the Vaishnavite Raas Lila tradition.

 

• Sattriya (Option 4): A classical dance form from Assam, originating in the Vaishnavite monasteries (Sattras) established by Sankaradeva.

question: When was the Secretary of State for India made responsible for the Government of British India by bringing about changes in the Home Government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1858.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Government of India Act, 1858, passed after the Revolt of 1857, transferred the administration of India from the East India Company to the British Crown. (भारत शासन अधिनियम 1858 — सचिव-ए-स्टेट)

 

• It created the post of Secretary of State for India, a member of the British Cabinet, who was made responsible to the British Parliament for the governance of India.

 

• The Secretary of State was assisted by a 15-member Council of India (advisory body) in London.

 

• The Act also abolished the Board of Control and Court of Directors of the East India Company, and the Governor-General of India was given the additional title of Viceroy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Canning was the Governor-General at the time of transfer and became India's first Viceroy.

 

• The Act of 1858 is also known as the "Act for the Better Government of India".

 

NOTE

 

• 1833 (Option 2): The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India and centralised legislative powers, but did not create the office of Secretary of State.

 

• 1857 (Option 3): This marks the year of the Revolt of 1857, which triggered the transfer of power, but the actual administrative change came via the 1858 Act.

 

• 1813 (Option 4): The Charter Act of 1813 ended the East India Company's trade monopoly (except tea and China trade), unrelated to the Secretary of State's creation.

question: Which waterway provides connectivity with mainland India through the India-Bangladesh Protocol route?
solution_text:
The correct answer is NW-2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Waterway-2 (NW-2), on the Brahmaputra River (Sadiya-Dhubri stretch, Assam), provides connectivity to the North-Eastern states with mainland India through the India-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP) route. (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग-2 — ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी)

 

• Under the Protocol on Inland Water Transit and Trade (PIWTT) between India and Bangladesh, cargo moves from the Ganga (NW-1) through Bangladesh's rivers to the Brahmaputra (NW-2), linking the North-East with the rest of India.

 

• A landmark cargo movement in 2020 saw foodgrains transported from Patna to Pandu (Guwahati) via this IBP route, connecting NW-1 (Ganga) with NW-2 (Brahmaputra).

 

• This route reduces dependence on the narrow Siliguri Corridor ("Chicken's Neck") for connecting the North-East to mainland India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NW-1 runs on the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system (Haldia to Allahabad/Prayagraj).

 

• The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), headquartered in Noida, is responsible for the development of National Waterways.

 

NOTE

 

• NW-10, NW-15, NW-83 (Options 1, 2, 4): These are other declared National Waterways on different rivers/water bodies across India, and are not the waterway connected via the India-Bangladesh Protocol route.

question: In 2021, the Indian men's cricket team defeated Australia at the Gabba stadium in a Test match becoming the only cricket team to defeat Australia in Brisbane since ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1988.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In January 2021, the Indian cricket team, led by Ajinkya Rahane (as Virat Kohli returned home earlier in the series), defeated Australia at the Gabba (Brisbane Cricket Ground) in the 4th Test to win the Border-Gavaskar Trophy. (गाबा टेस्ट जीत — भारत, 2021)

 

• This ended Australia's 32-year unbeaten streak at the Gabba, as no team had defeated Australia there since the West Indies in 1988.

 

• India chased down a target of 328 runs on the final day, with young batter Shubman Gill and all-rounder Rishabh Pant playing key roles.

 

• This victory came despite India fielding a depleted, injury-hit squad, and is considered one of the greatest triumphs in Indian cricket history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India also won the preceding 2018-19 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia, becoming the first Asian team to win a Test series there.

 

• The Gabba Test win of 2021 is often referred to as one of cricket's greatest comebacks, given India's depleted bowling attack.

 

NOTE

 

• 1996, 1992, 1990 (Options 1, 2, 3): None of these years mark Australia's last defeat at the Gabba before 2021; that distinction belongs to 1988.

question: The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the ____ Amendment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 42nd.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution of India by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. (42वां संशोधन — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• They were incorporated as Article 51-A in Part IV-A of the Constitution, originally listing 10 duties.

 

• A 11th Fundamental Duty (relating to providing opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 and 14) was later added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• The 42nd Amendment is often called the "Mini-Constitution" due to the wide-ranging changes it made, including changes to the Preamble and additions to the Directive Principles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment also added the words "Socialist", "Secular" and "Integrity" to the Preamble of the Constitution.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are not legally enforceable in a court of law.

 

NOTE

 

• 73rd (Option 1): This amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.

 

• 34th (Option 3): This amendment (1974) placed certain state land reform laws in the Ninth Schedule.

 

• 44th (Option 4): This amendment (1978) removed the right to property as a Fundamental Right and made it a legal right instead.

question: ________ announced the bifurcation of the British Indian Empire into a secular India and Islamic Pakistan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Louis Mountbatten.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Louis Mountbatten, the last Viceroy of British India, announced the partition/bifurcation of British India into the secular Dominion of India and the Islamic state of Pakistan through the Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan), 1947. (माउंटबेटन योजना — भारत-पाकिस्तान विभाजन)

 

• This plan formed the basis of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament, under which India and Pakistan became independent on 15 August 1947 and 14 August 1947 respectively.

 

• The boundary between the two nations was demarcated by the Radcliffe Line, headed by Sir Cyril Radcliffe.

 

• Mountbatten served as the first Governor-General of independent India after partition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mountbatten succeeded Lord Wavell as Viceroy in March 1947.

 

• C. Rajagopalachari succeeded Mountbatten as the first Indian Governor-General of India in 1948.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Ripon (Option 1): Known for the Ilbert Bill and local self-government reforms; often called the "Father of Local Self-Government" in India.

 

• Lord Dalhousie (Option 2): Known for the Doctrine of Lapse and introducing railways and telegraph in India.

 

• Lord Curzon (Option 4): Known for the Partition of Bengal (1905), not the 1947 partition of India.

question: Which of the following cells are found in the liver of mammals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kupffer cells.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kupffer cells are specialised macrophages found in the liver of mammals, lining the walls of the liver sinusoids. (कुफ़्फर कोशिकाएं — यकृत)

 

• They form part of the reticuloendothelial (mononuclear phagocyte) system and function to remove old/damaged red blood cells, bacteria and other debris from the blood as it passes through the liver.

 

• They also play a role in iron and bilirubin metabolism and in the body's immune response.

 

• Kupffer cells were first described by German anatomist Karl Wilhelm von Kupffer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The liver is the largest gland in the human body and performs functions like detoxification, bile production, and metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

 

• Other specialised phagocytic cells in the body include microglia (brain), alveolar macrophages (lungs) and osteoclasts (bone).

 

NOTE

 

• Purkinje cells (Option 1): These are large neurons found in the cerebellum of the brain, not the liver.

 

• Microglial cells (Option 2): These are the resident immune cells (macrophages) of the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord), not the liver.

 

• Sensory cells (Option 4): These are specialised receptor cells found in sense organs, not specific to the liver.

question: Who is the first law officer of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Attorney General of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Attorney General of India (AGI), provided for under Article 76 of the Constitution, is the highest law officer and chief legal advisor to the Government of India. (भारत के महान्यायवादी — प्रथम विधि अधिकारी)

 

• The AGI is appointed by the President of India and must possess the same qualifications as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

 

• The Attorney General has the right to audience in all courts in India and the right to participate in Parliamentary proceedings, though without a vote.

 

• The current (as of 2023) Attorney General of India was R. Venkataramani, appointed in 2022.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Solicitor General of India assists the Attorney General but is not a constitutional post — it is a statutory position.

 

• Each state has an Advocate General, under Article 165, who is the highest law officer at the state level.

 

NOTE

 

• Advocate General of State (Option 1): This is the highest law officer at the state, not the national, level (Article 165).

 

• Chief Justice of India (Option 2): Heads the judiciary (Supreme Court) but is not termed the "first law officer" of India.

 

• Minister of Law (Option 4): A political/Cabinet post responsible for the Law Ministry, not a constitutional law officer post.

question: The Shailendra kings who founded their empire in South-east Asia in the 8th Century AD were the followers of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Buddhism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Shailendra dynasty, which established its empire in Java, Indonesia (South-East Asia) in the 8th century AD, were devout followers of Mahayana Buddhism. (शैलेंद्र वंश — महायान बौद्ध धर्म)

 

• They are best known for constructing the magnificent Borobudur temple, the largest Buddhist monument in the world, located in Central Java.

 

• The Shailendras had close cultural and trade links with the Pala dynasty of Bengal/Bihar, another major patron of Mahayana Buddhism at the time.

 

• Their empire also extended influence over the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, contributing to the spread of Indian culture and Buddhism in South-East Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Shailendras later merged with, or were succeeded by, the Hindu Mataram Kingdom and subsequently the Srivijaya Empire of Sumatra.

 

• Borobudur was built around 780-840 AD and was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1991.

 

NOTE

 

• Shaivism (Option 2): This Shiva-worshipping tradition was followed by other South-East Asian dynasties like the Sailendras' contemporaries in the Mataram kingdom (e.g., builders of Prambanan), not the Shailendras themselves.

 

• Jainism (Option 3): Jainism had limited spread in South-East Asia and was not the faith of the Shailendra kings.

 

• Hinduism (Option 4): While Hinduism was influential in the region overall (e.g. later Mataram/Prambanan builders), the Shailendra dynasty specifically patronised Buddhism.

question: Which Vitamin D analogue is used to treat hypoparathyroidism, refractory rickets and familial hypophosphatemia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ergocalciferol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ergocalciferol (Vitamin D2) is a Vitamin D analogue used therapeutically to treat conditions like hypoparathyroidism, refractory (Vitamin D-resistant) rickets and familial hypophosphatemia. (एर्गोकैल्सिफेरॉल — विटामिन D2)

 

• It works by promoting intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate, helping regulate bone mineralisation.

 

• Ergocalciferol is produced by the UV irradiation of ergosterol, found in fungi/yeast, and is one of the two major dietary forms of Vitamin D (the other being cholecalciferol, Vitamin D3).

 

• It is often prescribed in high doses for these specific bone/mineral metabolism disorders under medical supervision.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) is the form naturally synthesised in human skin upon exposure to sunlight.

 

• Vitamin D deficiency in children causes rickets, while in adults it causes osteomalacia.

 

NOTE

 

• Tacalcitol (Option 1): This is a synthetic Vitamin D3 analogue used mainly as a topical treatment for psoriasis, not for these systemic bone disorders.

 

• Tocopherol (Option 2): This is another name for Vitamin E, unrelated to Vitamin D or these conditions.

 

• Retinol (Option 4): This is a form of Vitamin A, important for vision, not related to calcium/phosphate metabolism.

question: Which of the following is NOT a type of rock?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Trace rock.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rocks are classified into three main types based on their mode of formation: Igneous, Sedimentary, and Metamorphic. "Trace rock" is not a recognised geological classification of rock. (शैल के प्रकार — आग्नेय, अवसादी, कायांतरित)

 

• Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling and solidification of magma or lava (e.g., granite, basalt).

 

• Sedimentary rocks are formed by the deposition and compaction of sediments over time (e.g., sandstone, limestone).

 

• Metamorphic rocks are formed when existing rocks undergo change due to heat, pressure, or chemically active fluids (e.g., marble from limestone, slate from shale).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The continuous process by which rocks change from one type to another is called the "Rock Cycle".

 

• Fossil fuels like coal and petroleum are typically associated with sedimentary rock formations.

 

NOTE

 

• Igneous rock (Option 1): This is a genuine, recognised type of rock formed from cooled magma/lava.

 

• Metamorphic rock (Option 3): This is a genuine, recognised type of rock formed by transformation of existing rocks.

 

• Sedimentary rock (Option 4): This is a genuine, recognised type of rock formed from compacted sediments.

question: Whom among the following players is associated with Javelin throw?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neeraj Chopra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Neeraj Chopra is an Indian javelin throw athlete who won India's first-ever Olympic gold medal in athletics at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. (नीरज चोपड़ा — भाला फेंक)

 

• He also won the gold medal at the 2023 World Athletics Championships in Budapest, becoming the first Indian to win a World Championship gold in athletics.

 

• He hails from Panipat, Haryana, and holds the national record in javelin throw.

 

• He was honoured with the Khel Ratna Award (2021) and Padma Shri (2018) for his achievements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neeraj Chopra also won a silver medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics in javelin throw.

 

• He is a Subedar in the Indian Army, having joined via the Mission Olympic Wing.

 

NOTE

 

• Pankaj Advani (Option 2): A multiple-time world champion in billiards and snooker.

 

• Saurabh Chaudhary (Option 3): An Indian shooter, specialising in the 10m Air Pistol event.

 

• Manika Batra (Option 4): An Indian table tennis player.

question: From which Latin word is the s block element calcium derived?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calx.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The name "Calcium" is derived from the Latin word "Calx", meaning "lime" (referring to limestone/calcium oxide). (कैल्शियम — लैटिन शब्द "कैल्क्स")

 

• Calcium (symbol Ca, atomic number 20) is an s-block element, belonging to Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) of the Periodic Table.

 

• It was first isolated by the English chemist Sir Humphry Davy in 1808 through electrolysis of a mixture of lime and mercuric oxide.

 

• Calcium is essential for bones and teeth, and is the fifth most abundant element in the Earth's crust.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other alkaline earth metals include Beryllium, Magnesium, Strontium, Barium and Radium.

 

• Common calcium compounds include calcium carbonate (limestone/marble) and calcium oxide (quicklime).

 

NOTE

 

• Calum, Coleus, Calcio (Options 2, 3, 4): These are not the actual Latin root of the element's name; "Calcio" is simply the modern Italian word for calcium, not the Latin origin.

question:
Arrange the following Development Financial Institutions (DFI) in the correct chronological order, according to the year they were set up.

(i) Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI)

(ii) Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI)

(iii) Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI)
solution_text:
The correct answer is (iii)-(i)-(ii).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct chronological order of establishment is: Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) in 1948, followed by Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) in 1955, followed by Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) in 1964. (औद्योगिक वित्त संस्थान — IFCI, ICICI, IDBI)

 

• IFCI, established in 1948, was India's first Development Financial Institution (DFI), set up to provide medium and long-term finance to industry.

 

• ICICI, established in 1955, was set up with support from the World Bank and Indian industry to promote private industrial investment; it later became ICICI Bank.

 

• IDBI, established in 1964, was set up as an apex DFI under an Act of Parliament, initially as a subsidiary of the RBI, later converted into a commercial bank (IDBI Bank).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• DFIs were created in the post-independence era to fill the gap left by commercial banks, which were reluctant to provide long-term industrial finance.

 

• India revived the concept of a DFI with the establishment of the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) in 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• (i)-(iii)-(ii), (ii)-(i)-(iii), (i)-(ii)-(iii) (Options 1, 3, 4): These sequences incorrectly order the institutions; the correct order by year of establishment is IFCI (1948) → ICICI (1955) → IDBI (1964).

question: Who among the following was the chief guest at India's 74th Republic Day celebrations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Abdel Fattah El-Sisi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, the President of Egypt, was the chief guest at India's 74th Republic Day celebrations, held on 26 January 2023. (अब्देल फतह अल-सिसी — मिस्र, 74वां गणतंत्र दिवस)

 

• This marked the first time an Egyptian President was the chief guest at India's Republic Day parade.

 

• His visit also coincided with celebrations marking the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between India and Egypt.

 

• A contingent of the Egyptian armed forces also participated in the Republic Day parade for the first time that year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The chief guest at the 75th Republic Day (2024) was French President Emmanuel Macron.

 

• India and Egypt elevated their ties to a "Strategic Partnership" during this 2023 visit.

 

NOTE

 

• François Hollande (Option 1): Former President of France, was chief guest at India's 2016 Republic Day, not 2023.

 

• Cyril Ramaphosa (Option 2): President of South Africa, was chief guest at India's 2019 Republic Day.

 

• Jair Bolsonaro (Option 4): Former President of Brazil, was chief guest at India's 2020 Republic Day.

question: Which of the following sitar players was awarded the Bharat Ratna in the year 1999?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ravishankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar, the legendary sitar maestro, was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 1999. (पंडित रविशंकर — सितार, भारत रत्न 1999)

 

• He is widely credited with popularising Indian classical (Hindustani) music, particularly the sitar, on the global stage, including collaborations with Western musicians like George Harrison of The Beatles and violinist Yehudi Menuhin.

 

• He also received three Grammy Awards during his career and was conferred a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award (posthumously, 2013).

 

• Ravi Shankar founded the Kinnara School of Music and trained several notable disciples, including his daughter Anoushka Shankar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist, received the Bharat Ratna in 2008.

 

• Bhupen Hazarika, the noted Assamese singer-composer, received the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2019.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Option 1): He is a vocalist, awarded Bharat Ratna in 2008, not a sitar player and not 1999.

 

• Hariprasad Chaurasia (Option 3): A renowned flute (bansuri) player; he has not received the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Bhupen Hazarika (Option 4): A singer, lyricist and filmmaker; awarded Bharat Ratna in 2019, not a sitar player.

question: MUDRA is a financial institution set up by the Government of India for the development and refinancing of micro unit enterprises. The full form of MUDRA is:
option_3: Micro Finance Usage Development & Refinance Agent
solution_text:
The correct answer is Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• MUDRA stands for Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency Ltd., a financial institution set up by the Government of India in April 2015 for the development and refinancing of micro enterprises. (मुद्रा — सूक्ष्म इकाई विकास एवं पुनर्वित्त एजेंसी)

 

• MUDRA provides funding to Non-Corporate Small Business Sector (NCSBS) through various financial intermediaries like banks, NBFCs and MFIs.

 

• It operates under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY), launched to provide loans up to ₹10 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.

 

• PMMY loans are categorised under three schemes: "Shishu" (up to ₹50,000), "Kishor" (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh), and "Tarun" (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• MUDRA is set up as a subsidiary of SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India).

 

• Under the Union Budget 2023-24, the limit under the "Tarun" category was proposed to be enhanced to ₹20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid previous Tarun loans.

 

NOTE

 

• Micro Urban Development & Refinance Agency (Option 1): Incorrect expansion — MUDRA relates to "Units", not "Urban".

 

• Micro Finance Usage Development & Refinance Agent (Option 3): This is not the correct official full form of MUDRA.

 

• Medium Units Development & Refinance Agency (Option 4): Incorrect — MUDRA is meant for "Micro", not "Medium", enterprises.

question: The first Paralympic games were held in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1960.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first official Paralympic Games were held in Rome, Italy in 1960, immediately following the 1960 Rome Summer Olympics. (प्रथम पैरालंपिक खेल — रोम, 1960)

 

• These games featured around 400 athletes from 23 countries, competing mainly in events for wheelchair athletes, evolving from the earlier Stoke Mandeville Games for war veterans with spinal injuries.

 

• The Stoke Mandeville Games were pioneered by Dr. Ludwig Guttmann in England, starting in 1948, and are considered the forerunner of the modern Paralympic movement.

 

• The term "Paralympics" was officially adopted from the 1988 Seoul Games onward, though the movement traces its origin to 1960.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The International Paralympic Committee (IPC) was founded in 1989 and is headquartered in Bonn, Germany.

 

• India's best-ever performance at the Paralympics came at the 2020 Tokyo Paralympics (held in 2021) and was further improved at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.

 

NOTE

 

• 1962, 1964, 1961 (Options 1, 3, 4): None of these correspond to the year of the first Paralympic Games; the 1964 Games were actually the 2nd edition, held in Tokyo.

question: The suitability of post tensioning is good for:
solution_text:
The correct answer is long spans.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Post-tensioning is a method of prestressing concrete in which the tendons/cables are tensioned after the concrete has hardened, and it is particularly suitable for structures with long spans. (पोस्ट-टेंशनिंग — लंबे स्पैन के लिए उपयुक्त)

 

• It is commonly used for large-scale structures such as bridges, long-span beams, flyovers and large roof structures, as it allows tendons to be tensioned to suit large in-situ members that cannot be easily pre-cast and transported.

 

• In post-tensioning, the concrete member is cast first with ducts/sheaths for tendons; after the concrete gains strength, the tendons are threaded through, stretched using jacks, and anchored.

 

• This differs from pre-tensioning, where tendons are tensioned before casting the concrete and is typically better suited for mass production of shorter, factory-precast structural members.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prestressed concrete was pioneered by French engineer Eugène Freyssinet.

 

• Post-tensioning is widely used in constructing cable-stayed and box-girder bridges.

 

NOTE

 

• End spans, break spans, edge spans (Options 2, 3, 4): These are not standard engineering terms describing the suitability of post-tensioning; post-tensioning is specifically favoured for long-span construction, not these categories.
